scope: Add a bounded, actor-owned integer reserve ledger that is separate from facet charge, native energy/time wallets, elapsed time, TIM, seat dimensionality and closure/capability state. Freeze the null, load-v1 and grade-load-v1 arithmetic and one-use event identities before native integration. This batch validates accounting state only; FT5.2 must bind preparation and replenishment to actual paid native work, and FT5.3 retains the full frozen grid and recovery gate.

load-v1.replenishment_gain: min(8 - reserve, 2) per distinct configured token

grade-load-v1.replenishment_gain: min(8 - reserve, 2) per distinct configured token

rules: Reserve is an actor-owned exact integer in the closed domain 0..8, initialized to 4 unless an explicit grid value 0 or 8 is supplied. Load is a nonnegative exact integer. Python booleans are rejected as integers. Grade is an exact integer 0..3 only where grade-load-v1 independent completion requires it.

The only policies are null, load-v1 and grade-load-v1. Policy identity is immutable for a ledger and serialized in every checkpoint. The null policy records comparable events but has zero preparation, loss and gain.

Admission names one immutable demand identity and load, records reserve_before and the policy-derived preparation count exactly once, and never mutates reserve. A second admission under the same demand identity is rejected rather than rewritten.

Independent or supported completion names one admitted unresolved demand and resolves it once. Independent loss follows the selected formula. Supported completion loses exactly one unit when available under either non-null policy. No reserve debit changes native wallet energy/time or refunds prior work.

Interruption names one admitted demand and a globally unique immutable attempt identity. A non-null policy loses one unit at most once for that exact attempt; replay is rejected and cannot drain reserve repeatedly. Interruption does not erase the demand or make a route forbidden.

A replenishment event may consume only one exact token identity from the finite token inventory configured at construction. The accounting layer additionally requires a distinct external paid-A5 receipt identity and records it without claiming to validate the native operation; FT5.2 must bind that receipt to the actual committed paid uptake before any integrated replenishment claim. Reusing a token or receipt is rejected. Non-null gain is capped at two and at reserve eight; null gains zero while still consuming no token.

Zero reserve increases the recorded preparation obligation for non-null policies but never removes an admitted demand, route or capability. Reserve is neither affordability nor permission. This layer has no API that selects, deletes or marks a route forbidden.

Every event is append-only, sequential and records balance before, signed reserve delta and balance after. Preparation remains a separate non-wallet obligation. No event may take reserve outside 0..8, mint native wallet value, modify facet charge, change elapsed native time or rewrite closure/capability history.

Checkpoint restoration requires the exact policy, actor, initial reserve, finite token inventory, append-only events, demand state, consumed tokens, receipt identities and seen attempts. Restoration independently replays the event ledger and rejects any inconsistent derived state.

The independent auditor imports no ReserveLedger. It replays the checkpoint from exact primitive fields, recomputes every formula, balance, uniqueness constraint and terminal demand status, and rejects tampered deltas, token use, receipt use, preparation, grade or event order.

Acceptance requires the sixteen exact new methods, the exact one hundred thirty FT4 predecessor method identities, canonical and workflow isolation witnesses, registered fixtures, a strict source freeze and unchanged source.

Passing accepts the FT5.1 accounting-state contract only. It does not establish paid preparation or paid replenishment integration, select the release reserve policy, settle C13/TD4, validate psychology or complete FT5.2-FT9.
gate: Sixteen exact FT5.1 methods pass with zero failures/errors; the independent auditor reconstructs every event across all three policies; no free or duplicate replenishment/interruption loop is possible; reserve remains separate from native wallets, TIM, dimensionality and FT4 state; all 130 FT4 method identities remain exact; fixtures and source remain unchanged.
next: FT5.2 paid preparation and replenishment binding plus separate candidate dynamics interfaces
stop: Preserve failures; two gate failures after correction stops.
